Issued at 150 AM EDT Wed Jul 29 2026

Today-Tonight...A low pressure system drifts offshore from the
Northeast US coast today, as the Atlantic ridge axis remains
across the Straits of Florida. Locally, the tightening pressure
gradient between the ridge axis and a surface front sagging
through the Southeast will lead to breezy SW winds 10-15 mph, with
gusts 20-25 mph. Deep moisture in place over the Florida peninsula
and SW flow preventing the development of the east coast sea
breeze will support hot and muggy conditions across the area
today. The highest heat indices (up to 110 degrees) are forecast 
near and north of the Orlando metro, with a Heat Advisory once 
again in effect from 11 AM to 8 PM for areas of Orange and 
northern Brevard Counties northward. Elsewhere, heat indices 
102-107 are forecast to be limited by showers and storms this 
afternoon. Regardless, it looks to be another hot July day for the
area, with highs in the lower to mid-90s. Will see little relief
overnight, as low remain in the mid to upper 70s.

Coverage of showers and storms is forecast to be near to slightly
below normal today, as ridging aloft works to counteract mid- 
level troughing. Without the east coast sea breeze, CAMs suggest
most activity occurring as a wave of showers and storms, which
develops over the Gulf mid- morning, then pushes eastward through
the afternoon. The highest coverage is expected generally south 
of the Orlando metro. PoPs attempt to capture this, with chances 
up to 40% in this area. Can't rule out a stray shower or storm 
across the area today, so at least 20% exists area-wide. Similar 
to previous days, a few strong storms will be possible, with wind 
gusts 50-55 mph. Conditions dry out into the evening and through 
most of the overnight. Then, scattered showers and storms (30-60%)
are forecast to move southward through daybreak, mainly north of 
I-4, as the front continues southward. Lingering dry air in the 
mid levels will again support the risk for a few strong storms, 
even overnight tonight.

Thursday-Saturday...A pattern change ends the week, as the surface
frontal boundary stalls in the vicinity of north Florida. Aloft, a
mid/upper level trough digs farther southward towards the
peninsula, as it moves offshore into the Atlantic. While it moves
seaward into the weekend, a series of mid-level shortwaves look to
traverse the local area. Upper level support, the nearby boundary,
and deep moisture (PWATs 2-2.3+") is forecast to lead to high 
coverage of showers and storms. 

Models agreement is somewhat lacking in coverage at times, 
without a solid feature (like the sea breeze) to hone in on. 
Regardless, PoPs are forecast up to 60-80% and will be highest 
initially near and north of the Orlando metro, then spread 
southward into Saturday. While not necessarily a washout each day,
multiple rounds of showers and storms will be possible, 
especially during the afternoon hours Friday and Saturday. 
Convection is even forecast to continue into the overnight hours, 
especially from around Melbourne northward. Showers and storms are
forecast to begin the day on Thursday, tapering slightly into the
afternoon. Despite muggy conditions, lingering drier air in the 
mid levels will support DCAPE values 800-1000 J/kg. Therefore, 
gusty winds 50-55 mph will remain a threat, as well as lightning 
strikes. Storms will be efficient rainfall producers, with 1-3" 
likely in a short period of time. Any training storms or multiple 
rounds of heavy rainfall could lead to accumulating minor flooding
concerns each day. Most of east central Florida is highlighted in
a Marginal Risk (1/4) for excessive rainfall each day through the
period.

Breezy SW flow continues Thursday, with winds 10-15 mph and gusty
20-25 mph outside of convection in the afternoon. SW flow slackens
into the weekend, as the pressure gradient relaxes. Nonetheless,
breezy flow will limit or prevent the formation of the east coast
sea breeze each afternoon. High coverage of clouds and
precipitation will moderate temperatures into the lower 90s.
However, peak heat indices 100-105 remain forecast. At night, lows
remain in the 70s, struggling to fall out of the 80s at times,
especially in the Orlando metro.

Sunday-Wednesday...Upper level ridging develops across Florida
Sunday, as the Atlantic ridge axis shifts northward early next
week and drags a bit of Saharan Air Layer into the Florida
peninsula. During this time, the stalled boundary lifts northward
as a warm front, leading to prevailing southerly flow over the 
local area. With the boundary drifting farther away from the area,
will see PoPs trend nearer to normal (40-60%) early next week. 
However, deep moisture (PWATs 2-2.3") lingering over the area on 
Sunday is forecast to support an additional day of high coverage 
of showers and storms (60-80%). Convection is expected to peak in
